title: Passing the OSCE and Viva — A Method, Not Luck

hook.en: OSCE and viva exams reward a clear routine under time pressure. Learn how stations are marked, a simple structure for every station and how to practise so that you stay calm.
hook.ur: OSCE aur viva exams waqt ke dabao mein saaf routine ko inaam dete hain. Seekhein stations kaise marks hote hain, har station ke liye saada dhancha aur practice kaise karein taake aap pur-sukoon rahein.

goal.en: By the end, you'll read a station task quickly, follow a safe routine (introduce, consent, expose, examine, explain), manage the clock, and practise with a partner using a checklist.
goal.ur: End tak aap station ka task jaldi parhenge, mehfooz routine (taaruf, razamandi, expose, examine, explain) par chalenge, ghari sambhalenge, aur partner ke saath checklist se practice karenge.

text.en: An **OSCE** (objective structured clinical examination) moves you through short stations. At each one, an examiner marks you on a **checklist**: they look for specific actions, not for brilliance. Marks come from **communication and safety** as much as from technique. A **viva** is a spoken exam where you explain your reasoning aloud. In both, a **clear structure** gets marks even when you feel nervous.
text.ur: **OSCE** (objective structured clinical examination) aap ko chhote stations se guzarta hai. Har station par examiner **checklist** par marks deta hai: woh khaas amal dekhte hain, shandaar pan nahi. Marks technique ke saath **communication aur hifazat** se bhi aate hain. **Viva** zubani imtihan hai jis mein aap apni reasoning bol kar samjhate hain. Dono mein **saaf dhancha** ghabrahat mein bhi marks dilata hai.

text.en: Think of an OSCE as a **driving test**. The examiner is not looking for a racing driver but for mirrors, signals and safe habits every time. If you do the safe basics in the same order at every station, you collect the easy marks, and you have your mind free for the hard part.
text.ur: OSCE ko **driving test** samjhein. Examiner race driver nahi dhoondta balkay har baar mirrors, signals aur mehfooz aadatein dekhta hai. Agar aap har station par mehfooz buniyadi kaam ek hi tarteeb mein karein to aasan marks mil jate hain, aur mushkil hissay ke liye dimagh azad rehta hai.

steps.title: Read the task and plan
steps.detail: Use the reading time to underline the task, the patient and the time. Decide your first three actions before you walk in. || Task parhein aur plan banayein

steps.title: Introduce and get consent
steps.detail: Wash your hands, say your name and role, check the patient's name, explain what you will do and ask permission. These are almost always marked. || Taaruf aur razamandi

steps.title: Do the task in order
steps.detail: Position and expose the patient respectfully, look first, then ask about pain, then examine the unaffected side before the affected side, and keep checking comfort. || Task tarteeb se karein

steps.title: Explain and close
steps.detail: Tell the patient what you found in simple words, say what happens next, ask if they have questions and thank them. Keep an eye on the clock. || Samjhayein aur khatam karein

text.en: **Same routine, every station.** Introduce, consent, expose, examine, explain. A routine you have rehearsed frees your mind for the unusual part.
text.ur: **Har station par wohi routine.** Taaruf, razamandi, expose, examine, wazahat. Mashq ki hui routine aap ke dimagh ko ghair mamooli hissay ke liye azad karti hai.

text.en: **Freezing when you forget a step.** Examiners do not mark silence as failure; they mark safety. If you forget something, say "I would also check..." and continue. Never invent a finding.
text.ur: **Ek qadam bhool kar jam jana.** Examiners khamoshi ko nakami nahi, hifazat ko marks dete hain. Kuch bhool jayein to kahein "Main yeh bhi check karunga..." aur aage barhein. Kabhi finding gharh kar na batayein.

question.ur: Station ke darmiyan yaad aaya ke allergies poochhna bhool gaye. Kya karein?

text.en: Pause politely, ask now and carry on
text.ur: Narmi se ruk kar abhi poochhein aur jaari rakhein

feedback.en: Yes — safety questions asked late still earn credit, and silence does not.
feedback.ur: Haan — hifazat ke sawal der se poochhna bhi marks deta hai, khamoshi nahi.

text.ur: Aise zahir karein ke pehle poochha tha

feedback.ur: Imandari ahem hai aur examiners dekh lete hain.

question.en: How should you practise for the exam?

feedback.en: Passive reading does not train performance.
feedback.ur: Passive parhna karkardagi train nahi karta.

text.en: Rehearse stations aloud with a partner, a stopwatch and the checklist
text.ur: Partner, stopwatch aur checklist ke saath stations bol kar dohrayein

feedback.en: Yes — realistic practice and feedback improve performance fastest.
feedback.ur: Haan — haqeeqi mashq aur feedback karkardagi sab se tez behtar karte hain.

text.en: Practise only the techniques you enjoy

**Use the Virtual Patient and Skills Lab as stations.** Pick a case, set a ten-minute timer and talk through your routine aloud. Then ask a friend to mark you on the checklist and note one thing to improve. Three short practices a week beat one long one the night before.
text.ur: **Virtual Patient aur Skills Lab ko stations ki tarah istemal karein.** Ek case chunein, das minute ka timer lagayein aur apni routine bol kar chalayein. Phir dost se checklist par marks karwayein aur ek behtari ka nukta likhein. Haftay mein teen chhoti mashqein ek raat pehle ki lambi mashq se behtar hain.

question.en: Why do examiners reward a clear structure even when the technique is imperfect?
question.ur: Examiners technique kamzor hone par bhi saaf dhanche ko inaam kyun dete hain?

answer.en: A structure shows safe habits that carry over to real patients: consent, privacy, comparison, communication and escalation. Technique improves with practice, but unsafe or disorganised habits are much harder to correct, so checklists reward them heavily.
answer.ur: Dhancha mehfooz aadatein dikhata hai jo haqeeqi mareezon par bhi chalti hain: razamandi, parda, muqabla, communication aur escalation. Technique mashq se behtar hota hai, magar ghair mehfooz ya be-tarteeb aadatein theek karna bohat mushkil hai, is liye checklists inhein bohat ahmiyat deti hain.

beats.patient: In a shoulder station you forget to ask about pain before moving the arm, then realise it with 4 minutes left. You are nervous and want to skip ahead to the special tests.
beats.assessment: A missed safety step is recoverable if you act on it honestly; skipping the explanation would lose more marks.
beats.treatment: Say you would like to ask about pain now, do so, then continue with the same routine and finish with an explanation.
beats.reassess: You collect the safety marks late and complete the station in time.

text.en: **In real clinical exams, never invent findings or examine without consent.** If a station asks you to do something unsafe, say what you would do and why, and refer or stop. Patient safety, dignity and honesty are marked more than any technique. Look after your own health: sleep, eat and take breaks before an exam day.
text.ur: **Haqeeqi clinical imtihanon mein kabhi findings gharh kar na batayein aur razamandi ke baghair examine na karein.** Agar station koi ghair mehfooz kaam kahe to batayein aap kya karte aur kyun, aur refer ya ruk jayein. Mareez ki hifazat, izzat aur imandari kisi bhi technique se zyada marks hoti hain. Imtihan se pehle neend, khana aur break se apni sehat ka khayal rakhein.

summary.en: OSCE stations are marked on checklists of actions, communication and safety, so a routine earns reliable marks.
summary.ur: OSCE stations amal, communication aur hifazat ki checklist par marks hote hain, is liye routine bharosemand marks dilati hai.

summary.en: Use the same routine at every station: read, introduce, consent, expose, examine, explain, and watch the clock.
summary.ur: Har station par wohi routine: parhein, taaruf, razamandi, expose, examine, wazahat, aur ghari dekhein.

summary.en: If you forget a step, say so and carry on; practise aloud with a partner, a stopwatch and a checklist.
summary.ur: Koi qadam bhool jayein to batayein aur jaari rakhein; partner, stopwatch aur checklist ke saath bol kar mashq karein.
